description: Academic Research Skills for Claude Code: research → write → review → revise → finalize
summary: The thing I respect about this one is that it explicitly rejects the "fully autonomous AI scientist" framing and instead builds a human-in-the-loop pipeline for the research-to-publication workflow as a Claude Code plugin, with integrity gates that actually check for hallucinated citations, fabricated methodology, and claim-faithfulness gaps at each stage. As someone who grew up in bioinformatics where bioRxiv preprints become publications within months, the citation-provenance layer — locator anchors, a claim-audit pass that fetches the source and judges whether the claim is actually supported — is exactly the kind of small, observable guardrail that makes me trust an agent output enough to use it. It also composes naturally with what I already run: PenguPool routes sessions in VS Code, AgentOn Pocket kicks one off from my phone, and this is just another skill layer on top of Claude Code that handles the reference-hunting and formatting grunt work so the actual thinking stays with the author.
